meta.name: Create X thread variants from new blog posts with RSS and SocialSwarm

name: Turn every new blog post into X/Twitter thread variants

parameters.content:
## Turn every new blog post into X/Twitter thread variants

Watches an RSS feed and turns each new post into ready-to-post X/Twitter threads — three complete variants, each built around a different hook (curiosity, challenge, story), so you can pick the angle that fits.

### How it works

1. **On new blog post** polls any RSS/Atom feed and fires once per new item.
2. **Generate thread variants** sends the post URL to SocialSwarm, which fetches the article and writes three full threads from it. Every tweet arrives with its character count already calculated, so nothing needs re-checking before it goes out.
3. **One item per thread** splits the result so each thread becomes its own item — ready to loop over, filter, or send onward.

### Setup

1. Create a SocialSwarm API key on the [developer portal](https://social-swarm-main-aa77a19.zuplo.site). There is a free plan and it does not ask for a card.
2. On **Generate thread variants**, add a **SocialSwarm API** credential and paste the key.
3. Replace the feed URL on **On new blog post** with your own.
4. Execute once to check the output, then activate.

### Customization tips

- Switch **Number of Variants** to 5 for more angles per post.
- Set **Source Type** to `Text` to repurpose newsletters or release notes instead of a feed.
- Add your own node after **One item per thread** to send drafts to Slack, Google Sheets, Buffer, or X.
- A manual run processes every recent feed item — add a **Limit** node after the trigger to handle only the newest.

## RSS post → thread variants

Each new feed item goes to SocialSwarm as a URL, then splits into one item per thread. Add your scheduler or inbox after the last node.
